summary: RotaSat Cameroun is a decision-support tool that helps Cameroonian farmers explore crop rotations suited to their own field. The farmer picks a location on a map, describes the soil, and sets five priorities (water, fertility, erosion, market, income). RotaSat reads ten years of NASA POWER observations for that point and proposes three rotations over three seasons. Each rotation is stress-tested against three real observed years: a normal year, a dry year and a hot year, selected by percentile from the 2015-2024 record, never invented. Every score shows the NASA data behind it: source, parameter, period and value. The tool works offline as an installable web app and answers by text message in 160 characters. It supports the farmer's judgment and local expertise; it does not replace them.
details:
THE PROBLEM

In Cameroon, crop rotation is mostly decided by habit, while rainfall varies sharply from year to year. In Maroua, NASA POWER measured 856 mm of rain in 2022 and 640 mm in 2023. A rotation that works in a normal year can fail in a dry one, and farmers have no simple way to check before sowing.

HOW IT WORKS

1. The farmer clicks the map or picks one of three demo zones: Western Highlands (Dschang), North (Garoua), Far North (Maroua).

2. The farmer describes the soil (texture, pH, organic matter) and sets five priorities.

3. RotaSat fetches ten years of daily NASA POWER data (2015-2024): rainfall, maximum temperature, days above 35 °C, root-zone soil moisture. The rainy season and the number of crop cycles per year are derived from that data.

4. It generates every valid three-season rotation and scores each one on water, soil and nitrogen, erosion, market, income and heat risk, weighted by the farmer's priorities.

WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT

- Stress test on real years: normal (median rainfall), dry (20th percentile of rainfall) and hot (80th percentile of maximum temperature). These are observed years, shown with the method used to pick them.

- Explainability: a "Why?" button shows the exact data behind each score, for example "NASA POWER · PRECTOTCORR · 2023 Jun-Sep · 510 mm".

- Field access: installable web app that keeps working offline for saved zones, and a text channel that answers in one 160-character SMS.

- NASA GIBS satellite layer (MODIS Terra NDVI) on the map, with a date selector.

ROTATION RULES

Never the same botanical family two seasons in a row; at least one legume in three seasons; three different crops; a crop is excluded when seasonal rainfall is far below its water need.

TOOLS

Node.js, Express, plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Leaflet, Chart.js. No database: NASA responses are cached on disk. Server-side input validation, security headers and rate limiting.

LIMITS

RotaSat is not a forecast: it replays measured past years. NASA POWER is gridded data (about 0.5°), not a field measurement. Crop characteristics and water thresholds are indicative orders of magnitude (FAO) and must be validated with a local agricultural technician. Offline mode covers the three demo zones with default settings.

USE OF AI

The code and documentation were written with the help of an AI coding assistant, then tested by the team. The voice-over in the demo video is AI-generated (synthetic voice). No NASA data was generated or altered by AI: all climate values come directly from the NASA POWER API.

LIVE DEMO

https://rotasat-cm-production.up.railway.app/
